:::{#def-conjugate-transpose}
#### Conjugate transpose

The **conjugate transpose** of an $m \times n$ complex matrix $\matr{A}$
is the $n \times m$ matrix $\matr{A}^{\mathsf{H}}$
obtained by transposing $\matr{A}$ and then taking the complex conjugate of each entry:

$$(\matr{A}^{\mathsf{H}})_{jk} \eqdef \overline{a_{kj}}
\quad \text{for } j \in \{1, \ldots, n\},\ k \in \{1, \ldots, m\}.$$

The conjugate transpose of a column vector $\vecf{z} \in \mathbb{C}^p$
is the $1 \times p$ row vector $\vecf{z}^{\mathsf{H}} = [\overline{z_1},\; \ldots,\; \overline{z_p}]$.

:::

::: notes
@axler2024linear [Definition 7.7, p. 231] gives the same definition,
writing $\matr{A}^*$ for the conjugate transpose.
These notes write $\matr{A}^{\mathsf{H}}$ instead,
because $^*$ also marks optimizers, as in $\vx^*$.
:::
